opcode_table.unknown_policy: Legacy profiles reject absent entries. Default profile uses the bounded core/stack convention described in instruction_layout.

tables: u32 labelCount; (NUL name, u32 code-relative address)
header.padding: Only verified all-zero bytes after the count tables are accepted and preserved.
header.minimal_header_rule: headerSize == 4 is explicitly treated as a no-table header; all other headers require both counts.

boundary_evidence: Sequential decode using the versioned instruction layout from the parsed code base
All header-label and 0001 code addresses aligned and validated as instruction starts
001B/F4 terminal beyond the maximum entry/forward target
Every referenced string is strictly decoded, NUL-terminated, bounded and after the selected code end
Referenced pool minimum is an upper bound, not the code end
A second feasible terminal before the referenced pool bound is rejected as boundary_unknown
Code-like incomplete continuations and zero-high-word unknown opcodes in the boundary gap are conservatively blocked, never guessed as operands or hidden behind an early terminal
Append output is rescanned using the same public automatic scanner; no caller-supplied or cached code_length shortcut

strict.rule: Only provably literal, adjacent name/body arguments are exported. Any unmodeled value/arithmetic/load/call marks the pending window unprovable and blocks the member.

vntextpatch.rule: Reproduces upstream EthornellV1Disassembler grouping: 0003 pushes, 0140/0143 take the top operand as body and the next as speaker, 001C discards the callee and turns the remaining stack into options for _SelectEx/_SelectExtend, 007E/007F/00FE and terminals flush. No value or taint tracking.
vntextpatch.evidence_grade: heuristic; strictly weaker than the strict profile
vntextpatch.isolation: Recorded in manifest engine.variant; inject and repack read it back and re-validate with the same profile, so heuristic rows cannot be written as proven rows.

profiles.shared_structural_checks: Both profiles share header/boundary/target/pool validation and both still reject the old dialect opcodes.
profiles.deliberate_deviation: Old message/ruby/flush semantics remain blocked here. msg-tool explicitly handles 0145 as reverse-order message, 014E as ruby and 01B5 as flush; these are not upstream no-ops.

event_semantics.pairing: Name and message come from the same event, never persistent speaker state.
event_semantics.empty_name: Internal; omitted name, absent policy, null name_operand
event_semantics.empty_message: Internal; not exported, associated hidden name is not writable
event_semantics.duplicates: Preserved as separate ordered events and per-operand locators
event_semantics.dynamic_values: No VM evaluation; variable/load/arithmetic/unmodeled effects taint the pending reference window. Single-literal messages with possible dynamic names are blocked, never called narration. Two fresh adjacent name/body literals, without intervening incoming code targets, prove their own roles despite earlier numeric work.
event_semantics.ordinary_functions: A directly supplied non-choice literal callee and its arguments remain Internal even with unresolved numeric arguments. Its unknown return value is not treated as a static speaker.
event_semantics.diagnostic_layer: scan_v1 returns validated structure with JSON-serializable semantic_diagnostics and no partial events on semantic failure. export_v1 and patch_v1 propagate the first diagnostic code/offset/opcode. Structural errors and unknown opcodes still fail scan_v1 immediately.

writer.strategy: Append every changed NUL string, including short translations, and patch only its validated u32 code-relative operand.
writer.identity: Unchanged text keeps original bytes and addresses, while still traversing writer validation and rescanning.
rejects: empty replacement changing nonempty name/message role
writer.profile: Taken from the member manifest and used for both the input analysis and the output reparse.

dsc_encoder.basis: Written and checked against this package's own strict decoder; not a line-by-line transcription of msg-tool DscEncoder::pack.
dsc_encoder.shared_fact: The 512 code-length keystream is produced by one shared helper (_key_bytes) used by both reader and writer, so the two cannot drift.
dsc_encoder.code: Greedy LZSS over symbols 0-255 literal and 256+n match of length n+2, then canonical Huffman. Falls back to 512 uniform depth-9 codes when the Huffman depth would exceed 24.
dsc_encoder.distance: The 12-bit field stores distance-2, so distance 1 is unrepresentable and the matcher skips candidates closer than 2 bytes.
dsc_encoder.determinism: Deterministic for a given seed and input; DEFAULT_SEED is fixed so rebuilt members are reproducible.
dsc_encoder.self_check: verify=True decodes the produced member with the package decoder and compares before returning.

functions: build_archive(members, version, name_encoding, max_members, max_total_size, verify=True)
archive_writer.layout: signature, u32 count, fixed-stride rows (name, u32 offset relative to index end, u32 size, opaque extra), then stored members in caller order. Version 1 uses stride 0x20/name 0x10; version 2 uses stride 0x80/name 0x60.
archive_writer.row_extra: v2 rows carry 24 opaque bytes after the size field. Preserve them through IndexEntry.extra; only default to zero for new archives.
archive_writer.self_check: verify=True re-indexes and re-reads every member through archives/bgi.py before returning.
refusals: names that do not fit the fixed field or the name encoding
member count or stored byte budget
archive_writer.not_provided: No BSE or image encoder; such members must be passed through as their original stored bytes.

legacy_api.limitations_unchanged: Limited seven-opcode subset, caller-proven code length, fully covered nonoverlapping pool rebuild. Not an alias to the new APIs.

limitations: Headered Ver1 only; no V0 or automatic headerless fallback
Static event grouping, not complete BGI VM evaluation; the vntextpatch profile may assign a text role to a stored or computed value
Width-only knowledge does not authorize translating arguments of arbitrary calls
Unproven speaker roles and competing boundaries fail closed in the strict profile
Pool-like opaque bytes are preserved; they are not repacked or interpreted as additional game assets
The leaf writer strictly encodes CP932 by default. Chinese outside CP932 requires the common JIS substitution layer and a compatible hook/font, or a separately verified encoding patch.
No BSE or image encoder; repack copies such members verbatim
No GUI, external runtime imports, game execution or paid API calls
Loose-script loading is operator-reported (see load_rules), not reproduced by running the game in this package; the exact loose name and the override/caching rules are still unconfirmed
No game startup, font or save-file validation

instruction_layout.inline_operands: 13 core layouts: the same nonempty set as the legacy table (msg-tool V1_INSTS has 12 plus specialized 0003).
instruction_layout.core: Below 0080, accept only the bundled core layouts; reject unlisted core opcodes.
instruction_layout.stack: 0080..FFFF: one u32 instruction word, arguments supplied through the VM stack. No per-call registration.
instruction_layout.bounded_deviation: msg-tool skips every remaining u32; this profile rejects nonzero high words and unknown core opcodes and retains header/target/pool and ambiguity validation.
instruction_layout.diagnostics: boundary.opcode_layout and stack_extension_opcodes identify the convention and IDs absent from the frozen explicit table.
instruction_layout.semantics: Instruction width does not establish return values, stack effects or translatable text roles.
